mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior month compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 2.0% in a single month, it signals a tightening cycle that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.0%, or the Rank IC is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in payroll employment and decrease in unemployment rate indicates a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes characterized by high housing starts, consumer confidence in the housing market strengthens, leading to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of late-cycle expansion periods with HOUST above 900,000 units, or the Rank IC is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production over the prior quarter signals robust manufacturing activity, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO increases, or the Rank IC is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.0% in a single month, it signals economic weakness that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 5.0%, or the Rank IC is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand across multiple sectors, which accelerates economic growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST and RSAFS both increase, or the Rank IC is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes where the CPI exceeds 2.5% year-over-year, the Federal Reserve is expected to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of high inflation periods (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%), or the Rank IC is below 0.02.
